title: Home Purchase Agreement Terms — Security Deposit After Repeated Returned Payments
content:
**Clause 9.5 — Security deposit.** A buyer with repeated returns on a Home Purchase Agreement posts a security deposit with the replacement funds for a returned deposit payment. The count is of returned-payment fees charged on the agreement in the twelve months up to the replacement:

(a) where **three or more** returned-payment fees have been charged, **1.0 percent** of the contract price, rounded half up to the cent, is added to the replacement funds;

(b) where **exactly two** have been charged, **0.5 percent** of the contract price, rounded half up to the cent, is added;

(c) otherwise no security deposit is added.

**Schedule to Clause 9.5 (hypothetical contract price 612345.67).**

| Returned-payment fee charges on the agreement in the twelve months | Security deposit added |
|---|---|
| 0 or 1 | None |
| 2 | 0.5 percent: 3061.72835, rounded half up to 3061.73 |
| 3 or more | 1.0 percent: 6123.4567, rounded half up to 6123.46 |

**Notes.**

1. The count is of returned-payment fee charges on the agreement ledger, not of returns as such.
2. The twelve months run back from the date of the replacement.
3. The percentage is applied to the agreement's contract price, the base price plus the lot premium.
